flywheel-energy.alt: A flywheel spins counterclockwise on a fixed stand. Its center of mass does not move (v_cm = 0), yet every piece of the rim moves: velocity arrows at the top, bottom, left and right of the rim point in different, opposite directions, tangent to the rim. The wheel therefore has kinetic energy of rotation. A panel derives K_rot = ½Iω² from adding ½m(rω)² for every piece, notes it is a scalar measured in joules, that doubling ω quadruples it, and that moving mass outward at the same ω increases it.
